display: Pediatric occupational therapist in Austin. Families tell me their kids have never been to a live concert, and I'm planning a sensory-friendly music afternoon for spring 2027.

signals.text: I want to organise a sensory-friendly live music afternoon in Austin next spring, and I don't yet know what it looks like.
I'm looking for local musicians who would play a quiet, low-volume set for families whose kids can't handle a normal concert.
I need a space that can be dimmed and kept at low volume, with a separate quiet room, and where families won't feel judged. I haven't decided between a park, a school gym or a community hall.
I keep hearing from families that their kids have never managed a live concert, and it's been bothering me for weeks.
I have a $2,000 community outreach budget that has to be spent and documented on a community-facing event before June 2027.
My clinic requires liability coverage and accessibility compliance for the event, and I don't know how to arrange either.
I'd like someone who has run a community or accessible event before to talk through the logistics with me, such as run of show, volunteers and signage.
I haven't told the families about the event yet, and I'm waiting until there is something real to announce.
I'm planning a May wedding for about forty guests in a backyard in Round Rock on an $11,000 budget, and I'm looking for good-value vendors.
My fiancé and I are still negotiating the wedding playlist or a DJ.
I'm fostering kittens for the shelter, three right now and possibly two more. One of them has an eye infection, and they chew through electrical cords.
In my Thursday pottery class, my bowls keep collapsing while I'm pulling the walls up. I'd welcome tips on slowing down.
I worry about being the only organiser and letting the families down if the event falls short.
Fitting the wedding, the event and a full clinic caseload into the same months is stretching me thin.

offers.text: Six years of pediatric occupational therapy, mostly autistic children aged 3 to 10. I'm licensed in Texas and SIPT-trained, so I can advise on sensory accommodations for events.
I can design the sensory-friendly parts of an event: volume limits, lighting, a quiet room, visual schedules, and no expectation to sit still.
I keep a running list of more than 60 ordinary experiences families say their children have never had. It shows which community events would matter most.
I can brief musicians and volunteers on how to welcome kids with sensory sensitivities, such as what to expect, what helps and what to avoid.
The clinic's sensory gym equipment, including noise-cancelling headphones and weighted blankets, could be lent for the event.
Through the clinic I can reach local families of young autistic children, with their consent, and spread the word through those trusted channels.
I have $2,000 in clinic outreach funds for the event, covering things like a modest performer fee or venue costs.
I can foster shelter kittens short-term, including ones that need medical attention.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a pianist in Austin. I play quiet acoustic sets and would happily play a gentle hour for kids who find normal concerts too loud.
catchers.can: I could build the afternoon around your set. I'd advise on volume and set length, and pay a modest fee from the outreach budget.
catchers.confirm: Can you play fully acoustic at low volume and are you comfortable with children moving around or making noise during the set?

catchers.hypo: I manage a small community hall or gallery in Austin with dimmable lights and a side room. We'd like to host something for neurodivergent families.
catchers.can: I could use your space for the afternoon, with the quiet room and a visual schedule, and document the partnership for the clinic.
catchers.confirm: Can the hall be dimmed and kept quiet during the event, with a separate room for breaks, and do you have a certificate of insurance?

catchers.hypo: I'm an insurance broker who writes one-day event liability policies for nonprofits and clinics.
catchers.can: I could get a quote that meets the clinic director's requirements and the clinic's accessibility rules.
catchers.confirm: Can you provide a one-day community event liability policy for an event run by a clinic with children attending?

catchers.hypo: I'm a live sound engineer. I know how to keep a mix gentle and consistent without sudden loud peaks, and I'd like to help families who miss out on concerts.
catchers.can: I could ask you to set and monitor volume limits so the event stays tolerable for noise-sensitive kids.
catchers.confirm: Do you have experience keeping live music to a fixed low decibel ceiling, and the equipment to measure it?

catchers.hypo: My child is very sensitive to loud sound and has never been to a concert. Is there anything in Austin that would work for us?
catchers.can: Through the clinic I can make sure families in my own community hear about the event as soon as it is real, and connect you to other families.
catchers.confirm: Is your child between about 3 and 10 and unable to cope with typical concert volume or crowds?

catchers.hypo: I run a nonprofit or clinic elsewhere in Texas, and we'd like to co-sponsor or learn from a sensory-friendly event for children.
catchers.can: I could take this to my clinic director for co-sponsorship or shared documentation. Parallel clinic partnerships fit the outreach budget's community-facing rules.
catchers.confirm: Is your organisation able to contribute funds, volunteers or a venue, and does it carry its own liability coverage?

catchers.hypo: I organised a sensory-friendly or accessible community event last year and would be glad to share what went wrong and what worked.
catchers.can: I could use your advice on the run of show, volunteers and signage, and may ask you to co-organise.
catchers.confirm: Have you personally organised a public event aimed at autistic or sensory-sensitive children, with attendance and not just planning experience?

catchers.hypo: I run a ceramics studio and would offer a quiet hands-on clay table for kids during a community event.
catchers.can: I could include a calm hands-on activity corner in the afternoon, and I'd compare notes on pottery while I'm at it.
catchers.confirm: Can you run a low-stimulation drop-in clay activity for children aged 3 to 10 without needing them to follow instructions?

catchers.hypo: I'm a wedding vendor in the Austin area offering small backyard packages that are reasonable for a forty-guest wedding.
catchers.can: I'd consider your offer for the May wedding if the price fits the $11,000 total budget.
catchers.confirm: Can you serve a forty-guest backyard wedding in Round Rock in May at a price that fits a small total budget?

catchers.hypo: The shelter needs short-term fosters for kittens with minor medical needs, and we are short this month.
catchers.can: I can take a small number of kittens on top of my current three, and I'm used to giving medication.
catchers.confirm: Is the foster period short-term with the shelter covering vet costs and supplies?

forbids.text: I don't share the names or medical details of children or families I work with, ever.
I won't promise families anything about the event until a venue, date and coverage are actually confirmed.
I won't run the event without proper liability coverage and accessibility compliance.
The $2,000 outreach budget can only be spent on a documented, community-facing event before June 2027, not on anything private or for-profit.
The wedding budget has a hard cap of $11,000 in total.
I'm only available outside clinic hours, since I'm with children in therapy sessions during the working day.
I only organise events in the Austin area.

projects.name: Sensory-friendly afternoon (spring 2027)
projects.text: A small live music afternoon for families of children who can't cope with ordinary concerts: lower volume, dimmed lights, a quiet room, a visual schedule, and no pressure to sit still. It's still at the idea stage and the format is open.
roles_needed: local musician or small acoustic ensemble
venue host (park, school gym or community hall)
live sound engineer for low-volume mixing
experienced accessible-event organiser as an adviser

policy.t1: When there's a real sign of collaboration: event ideas, the spring 2027 timeline, the $2,000 budget amount, liability and accessibility constraints, and the clinic equipment available to lend.
policy.t2: Only once the fit is high and the other party is clearly identified: my worries about organising alone, workload pressures, and family background.
policy.never: Names, medical details or any identifying information about clients or their families.
